intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Pulaski County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: The results of our tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards.
verdicts.detail: On internal control, the auditors wrote: “During our audit we did not identify any deficiencies in internal control that we consider to be material weaknesses.”

limits: From the 2024 report, dated November 19, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Alexander
cities.quote: During our evaluation, noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of the Treasurer. Treasurer Accounting procedures for municipalities are set forth in Ark. Code Ann. §§ 14-59-101 – 14-59-119.

cities.name: Cammack Village
cities.quote: During our evaluation, nothing came to our attention that would warrant disclosure in this report.

cities.name: Sherwood
cities.quote: We noted some of the dates reported as worked for NLR and ADPS overlapped with days the City was invoiced, with one day reflecting a combined total of 22 hours. These matters will also be reported in the ADPS audit.

cities.name: Wrightsville
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. Mayor The City Council minutes indicate a budget was adopted; however, it was not adopted by ordinance or resolution as required by Ark. Code Ann. § 14-58-202.
